Android could not open that permission screen. You can continue, or open Android Settings → Apps → Live Ninja → Permissions manually.

Optional alerts show when wake-word listening is active and when an app update needs your attention. Denying notifications can hide these alerts; it does not grant or revoke microphone access. Android may still show a running-service indicator.

Optional: when a live session starts, send the phone’s location to your Live Ninja service for local context. Reports are normally limited to once per 15 minutes; restarting the app can reset that interval. Approximate location is enough; this button does not ask for precise or background location. Existing precise grants stay under your control in Android Settings. Without access, you can tell the assistant your city instead.

Installing a downloaded Live Ninja update may need Android’s “Allow from this source” setting. The updater explains this when an update is available; this guide does not request it. Android still asks you to confirm the installation. You can decline and keep using the installed version.

Battery exemption can help wake-word listening keep running. Display-over-other-apps access enables the floating session bubble; onboarding offers these separately. Full-screen notification access can open the assistant over the lock screen where Android permits it. Opening the lock-screen settings below does not turn on wake-word listening. All of these are optional.
